newsitem.title: UK: ABN Amro director offered Horlick job - paper.
newsitem.headline: ABN Amro director offered Horlick job - paper.

text.p: A senior director of ABN Amro has become the first within the group to admit he made a job offer to Nicola Horlick, the former Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (DMG) fund manager, The Times alleged on Friday.
The Times report said Rijnhard van Tets, a member of the managing board of ABN Amro, said he had approached Horlick about a job but did not try and poach her entire team at DMG.
Horlick was suspended by DMG on January 14 just days after being promoted managing director of Morgan Grenfell Asset Management amid allegations that she planned to defect and take her team with her.

The report quoted van Tets saying "I had a meeting with Ms Horlick about her herself and not her team. I am not a believer in poaching teams and I have never done that. Nor would I try to disrupt their business."

Horlick was quoted in the report responding "I did meet van Tets unexpectedly at the Lanesborough Hotel in London on the evening of Wednesday January 8. He basically said he would like me to run the global asset management business of ABN Amro."
She is trying to conduct a campaign to regain her job and has denied allegaitons that she tried to poach staff. DMG has said in the past it has no plans to compensate or reinstate her.
